sentences.zh: 所以，以源氏为例，显而易见的是，在小说进程中，他先后被称为——我随便挑几个读一下——

sentences.en: the captain, the commander of the right, acting grand counsellor, his grace, the palace minister, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 中将、右大将、权大纳言、殿下、内大臣，等等，等等。

sentences.en: And of course, he ends up as the honorary retired emperor.
sentences.zh: 当然，他最后成了名誉上的太上皇。

sentences.en: And throughout the novel, people tend to be referred to by their titles.
sentences.zh: 而且在整部小说中，人们往往都用头衔来指代彼此。

sentences.en: And this can be quite confusing because, you know, someone gets promoted midway through a chapter.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人非常困惑，因为你看，某个人在某一章的中途就升官了。

sentences.en: Oh, and their title changes.
sentences.zh: 哦，然后他们的头衔就变了。

sentences.en: Suddenly, quite difficult to work out who he is.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，很难弄清楚他到底是谁。

sentences.en: So, actually, we already do this, don't we?
sentences.zh: 所以，其实我们已经在这么做了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, we call him Theo when we're recording just to please the audience.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，我们在录音时叫他提奥（Theo），只是为了讨好听众。

sentences.en: But in reality, we just call him, you and I, when we're talking about him, we just call him the podcast producer.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们俩在谈论他时，只会叫他播客制作人。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's his name.
sentences.zh: 对，这就是他的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, that's who he is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我来说，他就是这样的人。

sentences.en: I've just saved him on my phone, on my WhatsApp.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚把他的名字存进手机的WhatsApp里了。

sentences.en: He just comes up as the podcast producer.
sentences.zh: 他显示的备注就是播客制作人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And of course, we do also have Tabby, but of course, Tabby is a woman.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还有塔比（Tabby），不过塔比是个女性。

sentences.en: Do you know how I refer to Tabby?
sentences.zh: 你知道我是怎么称呼塔比的吗？

sentences.en: So, Tabby, when she comes up on my phone, I just put, rest is history, foreign office.
sentences.zh: 所以，当塔比出现在我手机上时，我备注的是：历史其余部分，外交部。

sentences.en: And we will explain why.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会解释原因。

sentences.en: Because there are kind of slightly different rules governing how women in the Japanese court are named.
sentences.zh: 因为日本宫廷中女性的命名规则有着某种稍微不同的规则。

sentences.en: So, they have kind of a range of nicknames.
sentences.zh: 所以她们有一系列各种各样的昵称。

sentences.en: They don't tend to have titles.
sentences.zh: 她们往往没有头衔。

sentences.en: So, Genji's mother, for instance, who we introduced to in that, opening paragraph, she is initially called the Kiritsubu Intimate
sentences.zh: 比如源氏的母亲，我们在第一段中就向大家介绍过她，她最初被称为桐壶更衣

sentences.en: because she's sleeping with the emperor, so hence Intimate.
sentences.zh: 因为她和天皇同床共枕，所以被称为更衣。

sentences.en: And she lives in a section of the palace called the Kiritsubu.
sentences.zh: 她住在宫中一个叫做桐壶的宫殿区域。

sentences.en: And anyone who's familiar with the palace will know that this is, it's not a bad place to be, but it's not the best bit.
sentences.zh: 任何熟悉皇宫的人都会知道，这地方不算太差，但也绝不是最好的位置。

sentences.en: So, it immediately establishes her kind of position in the pecking order.
sentences.zh: 所以这立刻确立了她在宫廷等级森严之中的地位。

sentences.en: And then when she delivers Genji, her name changes and she gets called the Kiritsubu Haven.
sentences.zh: 接着，当她生下源氏后，她的名字变了，被称为桐壶殿。

sentences.en: A haven is a kind of unofficial place.
sentences.zh: “殿”是一种非官方的称谓。

sentences.en: Title for a woman who has borne a child to either an emperor or an heir apparent.
sentences.zh: 用来称呼那些为天皇或皇嗣生下孩子的女性的头衔。

sentences.en: And literally, it means, I kind of read up on this, it literally means a place in which the august seed has found reSt.
sentences.zh: 字面意思——我专门查阅过——字面意思就是“真龙天子的龙种栖息之所”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, the feminist critics must enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 那女权主义评论家们一定很喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, if you are a haven, that's what's happened to you.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是一个“殿”，这就是你所经历的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But obviously, not everyone gets pregnant by an emperor.
sentences.zh: 但显然，并不是每个人都能怀上天皇的孩子。

sentences.en: So, not everyone's a haven.
sentences.zh: 所以，并不是每个人都能被称为“殿”。

sentences.en: So, what of women who don't have that status?
sentences.zh: 那么，那些没有这种身份的女性该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: You might be given a nickname that comes from kind of almost anything.
sentences.zh: 你可能会得到一个几乎可以源自任何事物的昵称。

sentences.en: So, Murasaki Shikibu.
sentences.zh: 比如紫式部。

sentences.en: Murasaki comes from the name of her heroine in the novel.
sentences.zh: “紫”字来自于她小说中女主角的名字。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: She's identified with Genji's great love.
sentences.zh: 她与源氏的挚爱联系在了一起。

sentences.en: So, that's where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以名字就是这么来的。

sentences.en: And Shikibu, it's the place where her father worked.
sentences.zh: 而“式部”，则是她父亲工作的地方。

sentences.en: So, he was a court official working in the Ministry of Ceremonials.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲是隶属于式部省的宫廷官员。

sentences.en: So, he's responsible for all the kind of parades and things like that.
sentences.zh: 因此他负责所有各种游行庆典之类的事宜。

sentences.en: And so, hence, that's why we call Tabby, rest is history, Foreign Office, because her father was a diplomat.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我们才把塔比叫做“历史其余部分的外交部”，因为她的父亲是一名外交官。

sentences.en: So, you're defined, if you're a woman, you're defined by your father's rank, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是个女性，你基本上就是由你父亲的官阶来定义的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is the case with this Murasaki Shikibu.
sentences.zh: 这位紫式部也是如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And she is very, very aware of the opportunities that are open to men that are shut to her as a woman.
sentences.zh: 她对男性拥有而身为女性的她却被剥夺的机会有着极其深刻的认识。

sentences.en: And she clearly has been since she was a child.
sentences.zh: 显然她从童年时期起就意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: Because in her diary, which you quoted from, her self-description.
sentences.zh: 因为在你的引用的她的日记中，有她对自己的描述。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's an amazing piece of work, the diary.
sentences.zh: 对，那是一部了不起的著作，那部日记。

sentences.en: And she wrote that for a couple of years in the first decades of the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 她在11世纪头几十年的几年里写下了这些。

sentences.en: So, while she is in the midst of writing the tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 也就是在她正着手创作《源氏物语》期间。

sentences.en: And she recorded this incredibly telling episode from her youth.
sentences.zh: 她记录下了她童年时代一段极其说明问题的插曲。

sentences.en: And it was when her brother was being taught by her father the lessons that would be appropriate to him as a boy who's destined for imperial service.
sentences.zh: 当时她的弟弟正在接受她父亲的教导，学习那些作为一个注定要为朝廷效力的男孩所应掌握的功课。

sentences.en: And Murasaki wrote, I was in the habit of listening with him.
sentences.zh: 紫式部写道：“我习惯于在一旁跟着听。”

sentences.en: And I became unusually proficient at understanding those lessons with which he was struggling.
sentences.zh: “对于他学得很吃力的那些功课，我却表现出异乎寻常的融会贯通能力。”

sentences.en: My father, a most learned man, was always regretting this fact.
sentences.zh: “我的父亲是一位博学多才的人，他总是对此感到遗憾。”

sentences.en: Just my luck, he would say.
sentences.zh: “‘我怎么这么倒霉，’他常说，

sentences.en: What a pity she was not born a man.
sentences.zh: ‘她没能生为男儿身，实在是太遗憾了。’”

sentences.en: Again, worth re-emphasizing, this is being written in the age of the Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 再次值得强调的是，这写于盎格鲁-撒克逊时代。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine if we had a diary like this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下如果我们能有一部这样的日记。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: Written by an Anglo-Saxon Mormon.
sentences.zh: 由一个盎格鲁-撒克逊女性所写。

sentences.en: I mean, it's unthinkable, but it existed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直不可想象，但它确实存在。

sentences.en: People may remember, we have the life of Edward the Confessor that was clearly inspired by Edith, his wife.
sentences.zh: 人们或许还记得，我们有《忏悔者爱德华生平》，这显然是受到他的妻子伊迪丝的启发而创作的。

sentences.en: But she doesn't write it herself, even though she's very educated.
sentences.zh: 但她自己并没有动笔，尽管她受过很好的教育。

sentences.en: No, exactly.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.en: Whereas Murasaki, you know, there's no issue with that.
sentences.zh: 然而紫式部，你知道的，这方面完全没有问题。

sentences.en: And it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太了不起了。

sentences.en: I think that, I mean, it would be anachronistic to call it feminist, but clearly the sense of resentment that men are monopolizing education.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果把这称为女权主义未免有些超前，但那种认为男性垄断教育的愤懑之情是显而易见的。

sentences.en: I mean, you get that through in China or in the Caliphate or in Latin Christendom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在中国、哈里发国或拉丁基督教世界都能感受到这一点。

sentences.en: But you don't have anyone, I think, as far as I know, expressing it quite so personally as Murasaki does there.
sentences.zh: 但在我所知范围内，没有任何人像紫式部那样表达得如此个人化。

sentences.en: So obviously part of this must depend upon her own personal qualities.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，这其中一部分必然取决于她自身的个人品质。

sentences.en: So you've mentioned them in your notes.
sentences.zh: 正如你在笔记中提到的那样。

sentences.en: The fact that she's very learned.
sentences.zh: 她博学多才的事实。

sentences.en: I mean, she's been listening to all the lessons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她一直在聆听所有的课程。

sentences.en: She's a very good observer.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常善于观察的人。

sentences.en: She's bright.
sentences.zh: 她很聪明。

sentences.en: She's determined.
sentences.zh: 她很有决心。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, all of those things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些特质。

sentences.en: Plus, she's in the imperial court.
sentences.zh: 再加上，她身处宫廷之中。

sentences.en: So she's able to reserve all this.
sentences.zh: 所以她能够把这一切都记在心里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: For why a woman is able to produce this at this point in time, at this place.
sentences.zh: 至于为什么一个女性能够在此时此地的这个地方创作出这样的作品。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I think there are kind of deep structural reasons for it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这背后有着深刻的结构性原因。

sentences.en: And they're well worth exploring, not just for their own sake, but because they tell us a lot about how Japan kind of emerges as a distinctive civilization.
sentences.zh: 它们非常值得探讨，不仅为了它们本身，还因为它们向我们展示了日本是如何作为一个独特的文明崛起的。

sentences.en: So just sticking to Murasaki for a moment, one of the nicknames that she's given at court,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们暂且把目光聚焦在紫式部身上，她在宫廷中获得的其中一个绰号是——

sentences.en: and it really upsets her because it's meant kind of mockingly, almost cruelly, is Lady Chronicle.
sentences.zh: 这让她非常心烦，因为这个绰号带有嘲讽甚至近乎残酷的意味——那就是“女编年史家”。

sentences.en: And the chronicles in Japan are the two oldest surviving texts that we have.
sentences.zh: 日本的“编年史”指的是现存的两部最古老的文本。

sentences.en: And they were written in the early 8th century AD.
sentences.zh: 它们写于公元8世纪初。

sentences.en: And the first of these was written in Japanese, and the second was written in Chinese.
sentences.zh: 其中第一部是用日语写的，第二部是用汉语写的。

sentences.en: And between them, they give a history of Japan that actually begins with the creation of the universe.
sentences.zh: 这两部书合在一起，提供了一部实际上从宇宙创造之初就开始的日本历史。

sentences.en: So a lot of it is about kind of the doings of the gods in the early years of the creation.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中很大一部分内容是关于开天辟地之初诸神的行径。

sentences.en: And it goes all the way up to the end of the 7th century.
sentences.zh: 历史一直延续到7世纪末。

sentences.en: And they are very clearly written to explain the origins of the imperial line, the line of the emperors, and to justify its rule as something that is divinely sanctioned.
sentences.zh: 它们显然是为了阐明皇统（即天皇世家）的起源，并证明其统治具有神圣授权的正当性而编写的。

sentences.en: So what you get from the chronicles is the fact that every emperor is descended from Amaterasu, who is the goddess of the sun.
sentences.zh: 所以从这些编年史中你可以了解到，每一位天皇都是太阳女神天照大神的后裔。

sentences.en: And this is something that is still part of Japanese imperial culture to this day.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，这仍然是日本皇室文化的一部分。

sentences.en: I mean, so Charles III doesn't boast about being descended from Woden.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，查理三世不会吹嘘自己是奥丁的后代。

sentences.en: But the current emperor, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但当今的天皇绝对会这么认为。

sentences.en: I mean, he's descended from the sun.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是太阳的后裔。

sentences.en: This is part of imperial ideology.
sentences.zh: 这是皇室意识形态的一部分。

sentences.en: And what we're told in the chronicles is that the first emperor, a guy called Jimmu, which I think is a great name, is the great grandson of the sun.
sentences.zh: 编年史告诉我们，第一位天皇——一个名字我觉得非常棒的家伙，叫神武（Jimmu）——是太阳的曾孙。

sentences.en: And he is sent down from heaven.
sentences.zh: 他是被从天界派遣下来的。

sentences.en: And he conquers all the various peoples of Japan, including men whose arms and legs are so long that people call them the earth spiders.
sentences.zh: 他征服了日本的各个部族，其中包括那些手脚奇长、被称为“土蜘蛛”的人。

sentences.en: And he reigns over Japan and he then dies at the age of 170.
sentences.zh: 他在日本统治，最终在170岁时去世。

sentences.en: And he is followed by a succession of 15 emperors, all of whom are very anonymous.
sentences.zh: 在他之后是一连串的15位天皇，他们都非常默默无闻。

sentences.en: They don't really seem to do anything except to have kind of madly, improbably long lives, kind of like the patriarchs in the Bible.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎什么也没做，除了拥有疯狂而不可思议的超长寿命，有点像圣经里的先知们。

sentences.en: They're living for kind of 400, 300 years, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们活了400岁、300岁之类的。

sentences.en: People do live for a long time in Japan though, don't they?
sentences.zh: 不过日本人确实很长寿，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, but not that long, not that long.
sentences.zh: 对，但没那么长，没那么长。

sentences.en: And when you add all these very long-lived emperors to the list of more recent emperors in the chronicle, so those who did exist, who are historical,
sentences.zh: 当你把这些长寿的天皇与编年史中更近期的天皇（也就是那些确实存在过的、历史上有据可查的天皇）加在一起时，

sentences.en: Japanese history is made to stretch back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 日本的历史就被拉长到了数千年之久。

sentences.en: And the reason that this matters is precisely because it doesn't stretch back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 而这件事之所以重要，恰恰是因为它的历史其实并没有延续几千年。

sentences.en: Ah, interesting.
sentences.zh: 啊，有意思。

sentences.en: It's actually very, very parvenu.
sentences.zh: 它其实是个非常非常暴发户性质的存在。

sentences.en: It's actually appeared very recently on the scene.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是最近才出现在历史舞台上的。

sentences.en: They're protesting too much.
sentences.zh: 他们这是在“此地无银三百两”。

sentences.en: They are protesting too much because the imperial family, until pretty recently, you know, a few hundred years before, had only been one of a number of kind of
sentences.zh: 他们确实是在此地无银三百两，因为直到不久前（也就是几百年前），皇室家族其实还只是日本中部、特别是大和盆地众多

sentences.en: great competing families in central Japan, and specifically the Yamato Basin.
sentences.zh: 互相竞争的强大家族中的一个。

sentences.en: It's the kind of southern central region of Honshu, which is the largest island.
sentences.zh: 那是本州岛（最大的岛屿）的中南部地区。

sentences.en: So the island that Tokyo is on.
sentences.zh: 也就是东京所在的那个岛。

sentences.en: Yeah, the middle bit.
sentences.zh: 对，中间的那块地方。

sentences.en: And even by the time of Murasaki, not all of Honshu had been conquered.
sentences.zh: 甚至到了紫式部的时代，本州岛也并没有完全被征服。

sentences.en: So the northern reaches were still kind of unstable.
sentences.zh: 所以北部的区域仍然处于动荡之中。

sentences.en: And Hokkaido, which is the northernmost island, kind of, you know, the barbarians were still kind of roaming there.
sentences.zh: 而作为最北端岛屿的北海道，蛮族们当时还在那里游荡。

sentences.en: So this is why it's incredibly important for the imperial dynasty and for the entire
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么对于皇朝以及整个依赖于它的

sentences.en: Japanese system that depends on it, to big it up as divine, as ancient, as universal.
sentences.zh: 日本体制来说，将其包装为神圣的、古老的、普遍的存在是极其重要的。

sentences.en: And so in the 7th century, you get this kind of ringing decree.
sentences.zh: 所以在7世纪，你听到了这样一道响亮的诏令。

sentences.en: There are not two suns in the sky, nor two lords on the earth.
sentences.zh: 天上无二日，土中无二王。

sentences.en: And this is aimed at the other Japanese families.
sentences.zh: 这显然是针对日本其他家族的。

sentences.en: There is only the one imperial family.
sentences.zh: 世上唯有一个皇室家族。

sentences.en: And in the middle of the 7th century, the Yamato monarch starts to call himself Tenno, which means heavenly sovereign.
sentences.zh: 在7世纪中期，大和君主开始自称为“天皇”，意为天之君主。

sentences.en: And by the early 8th century, what had previously been Yamato, so the region where this imperial family has come from,
sentences.zh: 到了8世纪初，原本被称为“大和”（即这个皇室家族发源的地区）的

sentences.en: is starting to be called the root of the sun, which in Japanese is Nihon, from which the English word Japan ultimately derives.
sentences.zh: 开始被称为太阳之本，日语中即为Nihon，英文单词Japan最终也由此演变而来。

sentences.en: So I guess if you know nothing about Japanese history, like me, all of this sounds pretty familiar.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，如果你像我一样对日本历史一无所知，所有这些听起来都会觉得相当熟悉。

sentences.en: It's not unheard of at all in Eurasian history for monarchies to become more centralized, more powerful.
sentences.zh: 在欧亚历史中，君主制变得更加集权、更加强大，这绝对不是什么闻所未闻的事。

sentences.en: When they do so, they develop a kind of cult and they develop a myth, a backstory.
sentences.zh: 当他们这样做时，就会发展出一种崇拜，并创造出一种神话和一个背景故事。

sentences.en: So Japan, in that sense, is maybe not massively unusual.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，日本或许并不算极其罕见。

sentences.en: And of course, Japan is being influenced, isn't it, by a neighbor?
sentences.zh: 当然，日本也受到了一个邻国的深刻影响，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Japan is not in a bubble and Japan is not the only country in East Asia that has an emperor and that sees itself as the center of the universe.
sentences.zh: 因为日本并不是生活在真空里，日本也不是东亚唯一一个拥有天皇且视自己为宇宙中心的国家。

sentences.en: And of course, this brings us to its colossal mainland neighbor, which is China.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也让我们想到了它庞大的中国大陆邻国。

sentences.en: And so you said, you know, this is quite a familiar story.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才说，你知道，这其实是一个相当熟悉的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, there are perhaps elements here of Charlemagne crowning himself in Rome and aping the titles of the emperor in Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里或许包含了一些类似于查理曼大帝在罗马加冕、并模仿君士坦丁堡皇帝头衔的元素。

sentences.en: But China is a much more domineering superpower than the Byzantine Empire is in the age of Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 但与查理曼大帝时期的拜占庭帝国相比，中国是一个更具统治力的超级大国。

sentences.en: I mean, it is the preponderant cultural influence in the region of Asia that Japan is attached to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是日本所身处的亚洲地区中最具压倒性的文化影响力来源。

sentences.en: And so that very decree that is issued saying that the Japanese emperor is the only sun in the sky.
sentences.zh: 因此，当年颁布的那道声称日本天皇是天空中唯一的太阳的政令。

sentences.en: I mean, that is lifted absolutely from the Chinese.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全是从中国借鉴过来的。

sentences.en: And the word tenno, the title that is often translated as emperor, this also derives from China.
sentences.zh: 而通常被翻译为“皇帝”的称号“天皇”，也是源自中国。

sentences.en: It's a Chinese word and it means the pole star, which the Chinese saw as being the throne of heaven.
sentences.zh: 这是一个中国词汇，意为北极星，古人将其视为天庭的宝座。

sentences.en: And so this being so, the Chinese, a bit like the Byzantines with Charlemagne, and they treat the pretensions of the Japanese with utter contempt.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，中国人看待日本人的野心，有点像拜占庭人看待查理曼大帝那样，充满了极度的蔑视。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a lovely story about a letter, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 对，有一个关于一封信的有趣故事，对吧？

sentences.en: I love this story.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the Yamato court sends a letter to China in the early 7th century, and they say the child of heaven of the land where the sun rises.
sentences.zh: 所以在7世纪初，大和朝廷给中国写了一封信，信中写道：“日出处天子。”

sentences.en: So again, that's this idea of Nihon, the root of the sun, sends a letter to the child of heaven of the land where the sun sets.
sentences.zh: 所以这又回到了Nihon这个概念，即太阳之本，写信给日落处的天子。

sentences.en: So that's China.
sentences.zh: 也就是中国。

sentences.en: And this is supposedly brought to the attention of the Chinese emperor who retorts, this letter from the barbarians contains improprieties.
sentences.zh: 据说这封信呈递到了中国皇帝面前，皇帝反驳道：“这封来自蛮夷的信件毫无礼数。”

sentences.en: Do not call it to my attention again.
sentences.zh: “不要再拿这种信来烦朕。”

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that's the Japanese kind of dealt with.
sentences.zh: 所以日本人就这样被“打发”了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But these rebuffs do not stop the Japanese monarchy from kind of aping the Chinese model.
sentences.zh: 但这些回击并没有阻止日本君主制去模仿中国的模式。

sentences.en: And in fact, from kind of consciously trying to model almost everything in Japan on the example of China.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们甚至是有意识地试图将日本的几乎一切都按照中国的样板来塑造。

sentences.en: So in the early 7th century, this kind of introduction of the Japanese monarchy on a Chinese model is termed by historians, the great reform.
sentences.zh: 所以在7世纪初，这种以中国模式引入日本君主制的变革被历史学家称为“大化改新”。

sentences.en: And as part of it, scholars and officials are sponsored to go to China to study it and then to come back and report.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，学者和官员被资助前往中国学习，然后回国汇报。

sentences.en: And they bring back Confucian ideals.
sentences.zh: 他们带回了儒家思想。

sentences.en: So this idea of, you know, a great civil service serving the emperor, a centralised monarchy, a meritocratic civil service,
sentences.zh: 也就是这样一个概念：一个服务于天皇的庞大文官体制、一个中央集权的君主制、一个唯才是举的文官系统，

sentences.en: you know, all the things that we're familiar with from Chinese history, but also with the literary culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所有这些我们从中国历史中所熟悉的元素，同时也包括文学文化。

sentences.en: So very rapidly, Chinese becomes, I suppose, what Latin is in kind of medieval European courts.
sentences.zh: 因此，汉字很快就变得像是中世纪欧洲宫廷里的拉丁语那样重要。

sentences.en: It's the language that anyone with any pretension to education, anyone with any hope of kind of rising in the service of the emperor has to be able to read and speak.
sentences.zh: 任何有点教育野心的人、任何指望在天皇手下高升的人，都必须能够阅读和说这种语言。

sentences.en: And when written Japanese is developed, it uses Chinese writing.
sentences.zh: 而当书面日语发展起来时，它使用的就是汉字书写系统。

sentences.en: So those chronicles, which are, you know, describing and praising the antiquity of the Japanese monarchy,
sentences.zh: 所以那些编年史，也就是那些描述并赞美日本君主制古老历史的文献，

sentences.en: first one's written in Japanese, as we said, but the second one is in Chinese.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，第一部是用日语写的，但第二部则是用汉语写的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's amazing that, you know, a patriotic history is being written in a foreign language.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，用一门外语来写一部爱国历史，这真的很神奇。

sentences.en: But I suppose you would write a patriotic history in Europe, in Latin, conceivably in the medieval period.
sentences.zh: 不过我想在欧洲的中世纪时期，人们大概也会用拉丁语来写爱国历史吧。

sentences.en: And that's the comparison, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是两者的对比，对吧？

sentences.en: You have the hegemon and its culture.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个霸权国家及其文化。

sentences.en: Well, it's hegemonic, hence the name.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是具有霸权性质的，所以才叫这个名字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And in the early 8th century, when the first permanent capital in Japan is founded,
sentences.zh: 在8世纪初，当日本第一个永久性首都建立时——

sentences.en: so up until that moment, the convention had been that every time an emperor died, the court would move to another location.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，惯例是每当一位天皇去世，朝廷就会迁往另一个地方。

sentences.en: But this is clearly not the Chinese way.
sentences.zh: 但这显然不是中国的方式。

sentences.en: The Chinese have a massive great capital, Chang'an.
sentences.zh: 中国拥有一座宏伟浩大的首都——长安。

sentences.en: And so the Japanese monarchy founds its own capital, which comes to be called Nara.
sentences.zh: 因此，日本君主制也建立了自己的首都，后来被称为奈良。

sentences.en: So again, in the region of Yamato, where the family had emerged.
sentences.zh: 同样，它位于皇族发迹的大和地区。

sentences.en: And it's directly slavishly modelled on the example of Chang'an.
sentences.zh: 它是直接且生搬硬套地模仿长安的样板建造的。

sentences.en: It has this kind of grid system.
sentences.zh: 它采用了这种棋盘格的街道系统。

sentences.en: Large numbers of immigrants are invited over from China and from Korea.
sentences.zh: 大批来自中国和朝鲜的移民被邀请过来。

sentences.en: So these are not just scholars.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人不仅仅是学者。

sentences.en: They're also artists, architects, dancers, musicians, writers, complete Sinomania.
sentences.zh: 他们还有艺术家、建筑师、舞蹈家、音乐家、作家，这简直是一种狂热的“中国崇拜”。

sentences.en: And in fact, people who want to study early Chinese dance or music, because so much of this was wiped out by the Mongols in China itself, if they wanted to learn about it,
sentences.zh: 事实上，那些想要研究古代中国舞蹈或音乐的人——因为这些在中国本土已经被蒙古人毁灭得所剩无几——如果他们想了解这些，

sentences.en: they look at Japan, where it was kind of better preserved.
sentences.zh: 就得去观察日本，因为那里保存得相对更好。

sentences.en: And just to quote Ivan Morris, who's written a brilliant book on the tale of Genji, The World of the Shining Prince.
sentences.zh: 引用一下伊万·莫里斯的话，他写过一本关于《源氏物语》的精彩著作《辉煌王子的一天》（译者注：原文为The World of the Shining Prince）。

sentences.en: I mean, he writes,
sentences.zh: 我是说，他写道：

sentences.en: Rarely in the history of the world has a country entirely free from external pressure, as Japan was during this time, so avidly acquired the fruits of an alien culture.
sentences.zh: “在世界历史上，一个完全不受外部压力影响的国家——就像当时的日本一样——如此热切地汲取异域文化的果实，这种情况极为罕见。”

sentences.en: And I guess the only other real example would be the Meiji Restoration, which is when Japan had shut itself off from the world for, what, 250 years?
sentences.zh: 我想另一个真正的例子大概就是明治维新了，当时日本把自己对世界关闭了，大概有250年之久？

sentences.en: And then in the 19th century, it opens itself up to the world of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 然后在19世纪，它又重新向西方世界敞开了大门。

sentences.en: But Japan doesn't become a new China, does it?
sentences.zh: 但日本并没有变成另一个中国，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's got its own resilient national culture and sense of national distinctiveness.
sentences.zh: 因为它拥有自己坚韧的民族文化和强烈的民族独特性意识。

sentences.en: And there's a sort of, you know, there's a tension there, right?
sentences.zh: 这里其实存在着一种张力，对吧？

sentences.en: That the Japanese are both copying China, but also they are very conscious of their own Japanese-ness.
sentences.zh: 一方面日本人在模仿中国，但另一方面他们又对自身的“日本属性”有着清醒的认识。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also there's kind of massive pressures on society because the nobility haven't gone away.
sentences.zh: 而且社会上也存在巨大的压力，因为贵族阶层并没有消失。

sentences.en: And the Confucian supposedly meritocratic bureaucracy gets set up.
sentences.zh: 儒家那套据称是唯才是举的官僚体制虽然建立起来了。

sentences.en: But the nobles aren't interested in this at all.
sentences.zh: 但贵族们对这一套根本不感兴趣。

sentences.en: You know, they're not going to subordinate themselves to a load of civil servants who've passed an exam.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们才不会向一帮通过考试上来的文官低头俯首。

sentences.en: And so throughout the 8th century, while the monarchy is resident in Nara, they are furiously competing with one another, not to overthrow the monarchy, but to dominate it.
sentences.zh: 因此在整个8世纪，当天皇居住在奈良时，贵族们在疯狂地互相竞争，目的不是推翻皇室，而是控制皇室。

sentences.en: And the way they do this is they're all competing to try and marry off their daughters to the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们实现这一目的的方法，就是争先恐后地把自己的女儿嫁给天皇。

sentences.en: You know, and if the emperor then has a son, their son will become emperor.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果天皇随后生了个儿子，那么这个儿子就会成为天皇。

sentences.en: And it breeds kind of escalating factionalism on the streets.
sentences.zh: 这就助长了街头不断升级的派系斗争。

sentences.en: The emperor finds it very difficult to keep control.
sentences.zh: 天皇发现要维持控制非常困难。

sentences.en: And he finds his own authority being submerged by the kind of the intensity of noble factionalism.
sentences.zh: 他发现自己的权威在激烈的贵族派系争斗中被逐渐淹没。

sentences.en: So in the 790s, an emperor called Kanmu decides enough is enough.
sentences.zh: 所以在790年代，一位名叫桓武的天皇决定：够了。

sentences.en: You know, Nara is hopeless.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，奈良已经没救了。

sentences.en: We can't maintain our control here.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里无法维持控制。

sentences.en: So we're going and found a new monarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要离开这里，建立一个新的都城。

sentences.en: It's actually rather like Louis XIV abandoning Paris.
sentences.zh: 这其实有点像路易十四抛弃巴黎。

sentences.en: And, you know, he comes across the site of Versailles when he's out hunting.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是在外出打猎时偶然发现了凡尔赛这块地皮。

sentences.en: And Kanmu likewise comes across the site where he wants to plant his new capital while he is out hunting.
sentences.zh: 桓武也是如此，他是在外出打猎时偶然发现了想要建立新都的地点。

sentences.en: And it's a location that seems to him ideal.
sentences.zh: 这个地方在他看来简直完美。

sentences.en: So it's about 30, 40 miles from Nara.
sentences.zh: 它距离奈良大约30到40英里。

sentences.en: And it is defended to the north, to the east, to the west by mountains thick with trees.
sentences.zh: 它的北面、东面和西面都有树木葱郁的山脉作为屏障。

sentences.en: It's linked by rivers to the sea, very navigable.
sentences.zh: 它有河流与大海相连，水运非常便利。

sentences.en: The soil is very, very fertile.
sentences.zh: 这里的土壤极其肥沃。

sentences.en: And it's perfect.
sentences.zh: 简直完美无缺。

sentences.en: So Kanmu establishes his new capital there.
sentences.zh: 于是桓武在那里建立了他的新都。

sentences.en: He calls it Heian Keo, the city of peace and tranquility.
sentences.zh: 他将其命名为平安京，意为和平与安宁之城。

sentences.en: So Keo is city.
sentences.zh: 其中“京”就是城市的意思。

sentences.en: And this is the city that in due course will come to be called Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 这就是日后被称为京都的城市。

sentences.en: And Kyoto, or Heian Keo as it is at this point, it's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而京都，或者说当时的平安京，非常有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's very, very explicitly modelled on a Chinese exemplar, on Chang'an, the great imperial capital of China.
sentences.zh: 因为它非常明确地以中国的模范——中国伟大的帝王都城长安为蓝本建造的。

sentences.en: But on a much bigger scale than Nara.
sentences.zh: 但它的规模比奈良要宏大得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you have this great palace, which is in the north.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有了一座宏伟的宫殿，位于北部。

sentences.en: You have markets to the south, a bit like Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 南部设有集市，有点像曼哈顿。

sentences.en: And you have kind of great avenues and streets crossing each other at right angles.
sentences.zh: 你拥有互相垂直交叉的大道和街道。

sentences.en: It's supposed to be entirely symmetrical.
sentences.zh: 它本该是完全对称的。

sentences.en: In fact, it very rapidly doesn't, because it kind of drifts to the right and the left kind of gets slightly abandoned.
sentences.zh: 事实上它很快就变得不那么对称了，因为它向右侧偏移，左侧则在某种程度上被逐渐荒废了。

sentences.en: And I think that that's the kind of perfect metaphor for what is happening with Japan generally, that they continue to model themselves on China,
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是日本总体发展现状的一个完美隐喻，他们继续以中国为榜样，

sentences.en: but everything is being kind of transmuted into something kind of subtly different.
sentences.zh: 但一切都被转化成了某种微妙不同的东西。

sentences.en: So Chinese institutions do remain the kind of the great model of government.
sentences.zh: 因此，中国的体制确实依然是政府治理的伟大样板。

sentences.en: The prestige of Chinese culture remains paramount.
sentences.zh: 中国文化的声望依然至高无上。

sentences.en: Chinese merchandise continues to flood Japan.
sentences.zh: 中国商品继续源源不断地涌入日本。

sentences.en: But increasingly, people in the Japanese court are thinking, well, we've got everything that we need now.
sentences.zh: 但日本宫廷里的人越来越多地在想，好吧，我们现在已经拥有需要的一切了。

sentences.en: Again, a bit like Japan in the 20th century, having gone through a process of westernization, then thinks, fine, we don't need the Western anymore, we'll improve it.
sentences.zh: 这又有点像20世纪的日本，在经历了一个西化过程后，心想：行了，我们不再需要西方那一套了，我们要自己去改进它。

sentences.en: And exactly a century after the founding of Haiyan Kiyo in 894, the Japanese government therefore decides as a matter of policy that it will no longer send embassies to China.
sentences.zh: 就在平安京建立正好一个世纪后的公元894年，日本政府因此通过了一项政策决定，不再向中国派遣遣唐使。

sentences.en: Cuts itself off, rather as it would go on to do in the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 切断了与外界的联系，正如它在17世纪晚些时候将要做的那样。

sentences.en: So that by the time that Murasaki is born, the number of foreigners coming to Japan has kind of slowed to a trickle.
sentences.zh: 所以到了紫式部出生的时候，来到日本的外国人数已经减少到寥寥无几了。

sentences.en: And it's really telling that in the tale of Genji, actually, the only foreigner who speaks in the entire vast sweep of the novel is a Korean physiognomist, you know,
sentences.zh: 一个非常说明问题的细节是，在《源氏物语》这部皇皇巨著中，唯一开口说话的外国人其实是一个朝鲜相士，

sentences.en: who reads a child's future in his face.
sentences.zh: 他从一个孩子的面相中看出了他的未来。

sentences.en: And he's introduced to the seven-year-old Genji and says, wow, he's amazing.
sentences.zh: 他被引见给七岁的源氏，并惊叹道：哇，这孩子太了不起了。

sentences.en: But for some reason, you know, he's not going to be an emperor.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种原因，你知道的，他成不了天皇。

sentences.en: And this is one of the things that prompts the emperor then to do what he does.
sentences.zh: 这也是促使天皇做出后来举动的因素之一。

sentences.en: So that was set up this world of the future Kyoto, here in Kyo, and we've got the relationship between Chinese and Japanese.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是未来京都（平安京）这个世界的背景，我们也理清了中日之间的关系。

sentences.en: What does that tell us about Murasaki and the origins of the tale of Genji?
sentences.zh: 这向我们透露了关于紫式部和《源氏物语》起源的什么信息呢？

sentences.en: So we've compared Chinese to Latin.
sentences.zh: 我们把汉语比作了拉丁语。

sentences.en: And of course, the thing with Latin is that for people who are speaking it in medieval Europe, it is a marker of tremendous status.
sentences.zh: 当然，拉丁语的特点在于，对于中世纪欧洲那些使用它的人来说，它是巨大社会地位的象征。

sentences.en: And I guess that must still be the case in Japan, right?
sentences.zh: 我想在日本也一定如此，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And specifically of masculine status.
sentences.zh: 而且具体来说，是男性地位的象征。

sentences.en: So remember that passage where Murasaki describes her brother, who's clearly not as bright as her, struggling with his lessons.
sentences.zh: 所以还记得那个片段吗？紫式部描述她的哥哥——显然不如她聪明——在功课上苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: What he's struggling with is learning Chinese.
sentences.zh: 他苦苦挣扎的正是学习汉语。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Murasaki learns Chinese to a great degree of facility.
sentences.zh: 紫式部对汉语的掌握达到了非常流利的程度。

sentences.en: She loves it.
sentences.zh: 她热爱汉语。

sentences.en: But this is seen in the Japanese court as unladylike, almost as freakish.
sentences.zh: 但这在日本宫廷里被视为没有女人味，甚至有点怪异。

sentences.en: A lady who speaks Chinese is, you know, faintly off-putting to men.
sentences.zh: 一个会说汉语的女性，你知道的，会让男性感到有点扫兴。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so at court, she tries to keep her knowledge of Chinese a secret, which is why she's so upset at being called Lady Chronicle.
sentences.zh: 所以在宫廷里，她试图对自己的汉语知识保密，这也是为什么她被称为“文学馆女官”时会那么沮丧。

sentences.en: Because clearly her fellow ladies-in-waiting have discovered it and are kind of mocking her, I suppose, as a kind of nerd.
sentences.zh: 因为显然她身边的女官们已经发现了这一点，并大概在嘲笑她是个“书呆子”。

sentences.en: It's that kind of idea, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想就是这种感觉吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she's very upset by this, but, you know, she loves Chinese so much that she's not going to stop reading it.
sentences.zh: 她对此感到非常沮丧，但你知道的，她太喜欢汉语了，所以是不会停止阅读的。

sentences.en: And in her diary, kind of very moving passage, you know, if you have ever been a bookish child, you can kind of absolutely identify with it.
sentences.zh: 在她的日记中有一个非常感人的片段，如果你曾经也是个书虫似的孩子，你绝对能与之共情。

sentences.en: She describes how she copes with, you know, a sense of loneliness and unhappiness by raiding this great stash of Chinese texts that she's found a scholar has got.
sentences.zh: 她描述了自己是如何通过翻阅一位学者收藏的大量汉文典籍，来应对那种孤独感和不快感的。

sentences.en: And she says how much pleasure it gives her to read them.
sentences.zh: 她讲述了阅读这些书籍给自己带来了多大的快乐。

sentences.en: But then she describes, it's like, you know, a bookish child being bullied at school.
sentences.zh: 但紧接着她描述道，这就好比一个爱读书的孩子在学校里遭受霸凌。

sentences.en: The other women gather behind my back.
sentences.zh: “其他女人们聚在我背后议论：”

sentences.en: It's because she goes on like this that she is so miserable.
sentences.zh: “‘她就是因为整天这样才这么讨人嫌。’”

sentences.en: What kind of lady is it who reads Chinese books?
sentences.zh: “‘哪有正经女子会去读汉书的？’”

sentences.en: And when she goes on to teach the empress who she's serving, Chinese, again, they do it in secret.
sentences.zh: 当她后来教自己所侍奉的中宫学习汉语时，她们同样是偷偷摸摸地进行的。

sentences.en: And in the tale of Genji, she portrays the daughter of a great scholar who teaches her lover to do the same.
sentences.zh: 而在《源氏物语》中，她塑造了一个大儒之女的形象，并让这位女性教导她的情人做同样的事。

sentences.en: So that's, I mean, a real gender inversion, that it's the woman who's teaching the man Chinese.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是说，我的意思是，一种真正的性别倒置，竟然是女人在教男人中文。

sentences.en: But again, it has to be kept an absolutely kind of deadly secret.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这必须被严加保密，堪称绝密。

sentences.en: And the implication of this, that Chinese, its script, its literature is for men, means by implication that to write in Japanese is for women.
sentences.zh: 而这意味着，中文、它的文字和文学是属于男人的，也就暗示着用日语写作是属于女人的。

sentences.en: And by Murasaki's time, the Japanese have developed a kind of phonetic script.
sentences.zh: 到了紫式部生活的时代，日本人已经发展出了一种表音文字。

sentences.en: So hiragana, still called that to this day.
sentences.zh: 也就是平假名，直到今天还叫这个名字。

sentences.en: But in Murasaki's time, it was called anade.
sentences.zh: 但在紫式部生活的时代，它被称为“女手”。

sentences.en: So woman's hand, it's a script that is associated with women.
sentences.zh: 也就是女人的手笔，这是一种与女性联系在一起的文字。

sentences.en: Whereas Chinese characters are so associated with men that they are called otokomoji, which apparently, my fluent Japanese kicking in, means men's letters.
sentences.zh: 而汉字则与男性紧密相连，以至于被称为“男文字”，显然，我那流利的日语告诉我，这意味着男人的字母。

sentences.en: There's men's writing, Chinese, and there's women's writing, which is this kind of Japanese phonetic script.
sentences.zh: 这里有男人的文字，即中文，也有女人的文字，也就是这种日本的表音文字。

sentences.en: And presumably, as with writing in Latin, with the language comes a set of expectations and formulas.
sentences.zh: 而且据推测，就像用拉丁语写作一样，语言本身就伴随着一套期望和范式。

sentences.en: Yeah, of classics, of models.
sentences.zh: 是的，有经典，有模范。

sentences.en: So the men will write in a particular way, they will follow a Chinese model.
sentences.zh: 所以男人们会以特定的方式写作，他们会遵循中文的范本。

sentences.en: But I'm guessing the women, if they're writing in kind of hiragana or onade, women's hand, they can do what they like, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但我想象女人们，如果她们用平假名或“女手”（女人的手笔）写作，她们就可以随心所欲，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's no Chinese model.
sentences.zh: 因为没有中文的范本。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: There's no rules.
sentences.zh: 没有任何规则。

sentences.en: So they can do what they like, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以她们绝对可以随心所欲。

sentences.en: And it's clear that Murasaki is writing a kind of diary.
sentences.zh: 很明显，紫式部当时在写某种日记。

sentences.en: There's clearly a sense that the court is the great focus of attention.
sentences.zh: 显然有一种感觉，宫廷是人们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: And it's not much of a leap for Murasaki to say, well, I could make up a great courtier.
sentences.zh: 紫式部顺理成章地会想，好吧，我可以塑造一个伟大的朝臣。

sentences.en: I could make someone up and situate him in a kind of a world that's faintly removed from reality.
sentences.zh: 我可以虚构一个人，把他置于一个与现实略有距离的世界里。

sentences.en: And there it is.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: There you have the great novel that she goes on to write.
sentences.zh: 她后来要写的那部伟大长篇小说就这样诞生了。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: It's precisely because she's doing it in a woman's hand, in a form that has not yet been codified, as it were,
sentences.zh: 正是因为她是用女人的手笔在写，用一种尚未被成文化的形式在写，可以说是这样，

sentences.en: and for which there are no models that she can effectively invent the Japanese novel.
sentences.zh: 并且没有任何可循的范本，她才得以真正创造出日本小说。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The sense of an alien world being brought so vividly to life is just, I mean, it's unbelievably exciting.
sentences.zh: 那种把一个陌生世界写得如此生动的感觉，简直是，我的意思是，令人难以置信的兴奋。

sentences.en: And this woman who is so elegant, so brilliant, Murasaki hated her, perhaps unsurprisingly, because I think Murasaki,
sentences.zh: 还有这个如此优雅、如此聪慧的女人，紫式部讨厌她，也许这并不奇怪，因为我认为紫式部，

sentences.en: clearly you get sense from her diary that she's much more introverted.
sentences.zh: 从她的日记中显然能感觉到她内向得多。

sentences.en: And what's fascinating is that the rivalry between these two great literary figures, these two extraordinary women,
sentences.zh: 而最令人着迷的是，这两位伟大的文学巨匠、这两位杰出女性之间的竞争，

sentences.en: mirrors a very deep political rivalry at the very heart of the imperial court, the Heian court.
sentences.zh: 恰好反映了平安宫廷核心的一场非常深度的政治斗争。

sentences.en: So in the second episode, we will be looking at this rivalry, we'll be looking at the Heian court itself, the emperors, the ministers,
sentences.zh: 所以在第二集中，我们将探讨这种竞争，我们将审视平安宫廷本身、天皇、大臣们，

sentences.en: the extraordinary women who are at this court, and which, thanks to Murasaki, and thanks to the other extraordinary women in this period who are also writing,
sentences.zh: 宫廷里那些杰出的女性，正是由于紫式部以及这一时期同样在写作的其他杰出女性，

sentences.en: I think we know in richer and more intimate detail than any court in history that had existed up until that point.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对这个宫廷的了解，比以往历史上的任何宫廷都要丰富、都要深入得多。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Tom.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: So that book is The Pillow Book, and we'll be talking about that next time.
sentences.zh: 所以那本书就是《枕草子》，我们下次会谈到它。

sentences.en: Tom, thank you so much for that.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，非常感谢你带来的精彩内容。

sentences.en: That was absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 真的太精彩了。

sentences.en: Now, if you want to join our own imperial court, you can, of course, do so by going to therestishistory.com, and there you will find all kinds of perfumed and elegant delights,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你想加入我们自己的御前宫廷，你当然可以访问 therestishistory.com，在那里你会发现各种熏香扑鼻、优雅迷人的乐趣，

sentences.en: but you'll also be able to hear that episode right away.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以马上收听到那一集节目。

sentences.en: So, on that bombshell, Tom, alligato, and sayonara.
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这个重磅消息，汤姆，阿里嘎多，还有再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
